Adobe Blog, “Brutalist Web Designers Eschew Rules for UX Best Practices”

An early trade article that credits Pascal Deville with codifying brutalist web design and quotes his reasons.

Context

“One of the first people to codify brutalist web design was Pascal Deville,” creative director at Freundliche Grüsse and founder of Brutalist Websites.

Deville: many designers explain it “as a kind of a minimalist movement. They want to get rid of all the creative elements and stuff you can add to a website today.” Others come from punk or hardcore culture, “where things are very rough”.

Deville also calls it a push against UX design that “has become a style that is very dominated by how Google and Apple do stuff”.

The article frames brutalist sites as “rougher, more basic — and at the same time more difficult to navigate”, which mixes in the antidesign branch.

Why it belongs

Good for dating and for motive. Its description of difficulty belongs to antidesign, which NN/g (2017) later separated.
